findings.title: Leader commits a joint-membership entry without a quorum of the joint configuration (VecProgress cached commit)
findings.scenario: U1 (cached VecProgress commit) x U3 (membership change rebuilds progress)
findings.summary: The update routes leader commit through VecProgress::update, which re-derives its cached committed value only when an updated value crosses it and otherwise raises the value in place without re-sorting, while its prefix scan assumes values above committed are sorted. upgrade_quorum_set (run on every effective-membership change) replays old ids in ascending id order, so a caught-up lower-id follower tied with the leader precedes it; if that tied prefix is not a quorum of the new joint set, the leader's next in-place raise leaves the vector unsorted, and a later crossing acknowledgement makes the scan accept a prefix containing a node that has not reached the value. In a 3-node cluster where leader n3 removes itself (joint [{1,2,3},{1,2}]) the leader commits and applies the joint entry acknowledged only by {2,3}; the {1,2} component has no majority. Reproduced through the real runtime (harness/repro/t90_specula_joint_commit_repro.rs, 5/5); the identical schedule on the baseline revision does not commit the entry. With 5 voters (harness/repro/t91_specula_joint_commit_divergence.rs) the falsely committed joint entry is later overwritten by a leader elected from an old-config majority that never received it: node 3 applied (term 1, index 9) while node 1 applied a term-2+ entry at index 9 (6/6 runs; baseline passes).
